title: Correlation flow governs learning at criticality
authors: Andrea Combette, Nelly Pustelnik, Antoine Venaille
abstract: The initialisation of deep neural networks determines whether information and gradients can propagate across depth, yet a unified theory connecting these properties to learning dynamics remains elusive. Combining mean-field theory and random matrix theory, we establish a direct link between correlation propagation and the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) that governs learning in the sequential limit of infinitely wide, infinitely deep networks. Correlation propagation to infinite depth is possible only at a single critical point in the weight-bias variance plane. At this point, we show that the end-to-end Jacobian vanishes algebraically with depth, and use this to prove that the NTK becomes exactly proportional to the output correlation at infinite depth. This equivalence between information propagation and learning dynamics had not yet been noticed. We further show that orthogonal initialisation suppresses the leading finite-size corrections present under Gaussian initialisation, clarifying the respective roles of the two initialisation ensembles in this limit. These theoretical predictions are validated quantitatively on finite-width, finite-depth networks. Together, these results demonstrate that orthogonal initialisation at criticality plays a central role in controlling the asymptotic dynamics of deep learning.
summary: This theoretical work unifies information propagation and learning theory for infinitely wide, deep neural networks. It identifies a critical parameter regime where gradient flow is sustained to infinite depth. The key finding is the direct mathematical equivalence between the network's asymptotic correlation structure and its governing Neural Tangent Kernel.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a unified theoretical framework connecting information/gradient propagation properties of deep neural networks to their learning dynamics.
main_result: It proves that correlation propagation to infinite depth is only possible at a critical point, where the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) becomes exactly proportional to the output correlation at infinite depth.
method: The analysis combines mean-field theory and random matrix theory to derive recursive relations for network correlations and Jacobians in the limit of infinitely wide and deep networks.
model_or_system: The model is a deep neural network ($\Psi_	heta$) analyzed in the infinite-width (mean-field) and infinite-depth limits. The analysis focuses on how information propagates through layers governed by weight matrices and activation functions.
key_observables: End-to-end Jacobian, Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK), output correlation matrix ($\Theta^L$), and their respective second moments.
important_parameters: The critical point in the weight-bias variance plane; infinite width ($N 	o \infty$) and infinite depth ($L 	o \infty$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes specific moment concentration properties (e.g., empirical moments converge to ensemble averages) and relies on mild assumptions about the activation function.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the problem in terms of information flow and learning dynamics, deriving recursive relations for correlations and Jacobians using mean-field theory, identifying the critical regime where propagation is possible, and finally proving the equivalence between NTK and correlation at this critical point.
why_interesting: While focused on deep learning, the mathematical machinery—analyzing spectral properties of large random matrices (Jacobian/NTK) in infinite limits—shares strong conceptual links with analyzing dynamics in complex disordered systems or spin-glass models.
